success_criteria.description: All four districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All four districts have roughly equal population (within 15%).

character.name: You
character.motivation: One last practice map — bigger, four districts, and every tool on the table at once. Draw a legal map, read the result, and you're ready for the real thing.

intro_slides.body: This is the whole kit. Fairhaven is bigger — four districts — and nothing is hidden: the Map Validity panel, the Lean view, the County borders, and the election result are all here from the start. Draw a legal map and watch what it produces.
intro_slides.heading: Everything You've Learned

intro_slides.body: A legal map is the same as ever: four districts, roughly equal in population, each one connected. The Map Validity panel tracks both — even the districts out and keep each whole until it's green. There's no seat target; read the result to see who your lines elect, then submit. The campaign scenarios are where that starts to count.
intro_slides.heading: Then the Real Thing

narrative.objective: Draw four balanced, connected districts — a complete legal map — and read the result your lines produce, then submit. (No seat target; this is your last warm-up before the campaign.)
narrative.epilogue:
That's everything: pick a district and paint it, keep the populations even and each district whole, and read the lean and the result to see who your lines elect. You've got the whole loop now.
From here the maps come with a reason to draw them one way or another — a party to favor, a community to protect or split, a rule to satisfy. Same tools, real stakes. Good luck.
